speaker: Zira
text: Thank you for joining me today. Could you start by telling me a little about your role in the lab?

speaker: David
text: Sure. I'm a third year doctoral student, and most of my work focuses on how older adults use voice assistants at home.

speaker: Zira
text: That sounds fascinating. How did you get interested in that topic?

speaker: David
text: Honestly, it started with my grandmother. She bought a smart speaker and kept asking it about the weather, but it never understood her accent.

speaker: Zira
text: Really?

speaker: David
text: Yes.

speaker: Zira
text: So that experience shaped your research questions.

speaker: David
text: Exactly. I wanted to understand why these systems work so well for some people and so poorly for others.

speaker: Zira
text: What methods are you using to study it?

speaker: David
text: Mostly semi structured interviews, plus a two week diary study. Participants record short notes every time the assistant fails.

speaker: Zira
text: How many participants have you recruited so far?

speaker: David
text: Twenty four. We were aiming for thirty, but recruitment slowed down during the winter.

speaker: Zira
text: Right.

speaker: David
text: We also had a few people drop out after the first week, which was disappointing.

speaker: Zira
text: Did you notice any patterns in why they dropped out?

speaker: David
text: A couple of them said the diary felt like homework. Others simply lost interest once the novelty wore off.

speaker: Zira
text: That makes sense. Let's talk about your findings. What surprised you the most?

speaker: David
text: I expected frustration, but I did not expect people to blame themselves. Many participants said things like, I must be speaking wrong.

speaker: Zira
text: Hmm. That is a powerful observation.

speaker: David
text: It really changed how I think about design. The burden should be on the system, not on the person.

speaker: Zira
text: Before we wrap up, is there anything you would like to add?

speaker: David
text: Only that I'm grateful to everyone who took part. Their stories made this project meaningful.

speaker: Zira
text: Thank you so much for your time.

speaker: David
text: Thank you for having me.
